note: Original public summaries for the search-indexed course pages in /lernen/. Written for these pages; they do not reproduce lesson text or exercise names. Run npm run assets after editing.
hub: Deutschklinik is a German course from A1 to C1: grammar chapters with explanations and exercises, vocabulary topics with pictures and pronunciation, reference lists with trainers, a German dictionary, flashcards and games. Pick a level to see every chapter.

sections.grammatik: German grammar from the first verb forms at A1 to nominal style and comma rules at C1. Every chapter explains one topic and practises it with exercises; B2 and C1 chapters also have an animated explanation.
sections.wortschatz: Vocabulary topics for everyday life, work and study. Each topic has a word list with pictures and pronunciation, exercises, and words you can turn into flashcards with one click.
sections.listen: Reference lists for looking things up and training: irregular verbs, verbs with the dative, verbs with prepositions and more, each with a trainer.

levels.grammatik:A1: Your first steps in German grammar: present-tense verbs, word order, questions, articles, the accusative and dative, and the perfect tense with haben.
levels.grammatik:A2: Building on A1: the perfect with sein, two-way prepositions, adjective endings, comparisons and your first subordinate clauses with weil, dass and wenn.
levels.grammatik:B1: Intermediate grammar: the simple past, the passive, Konjunktiv II, the genitive, relative clauses, infinitive clauses and connectors for longer sentences.
levels.grammatik:B2: Upper-intermediate grammar in depth: word order, Konjunktiv II, the passive, prepositions, reported speech, subordinate clauses and fixed word combinations – each chapter with an animated explanation.
levels.grammatik:C1: Advanced grammar for precise and formal German: information structure, passive alternatives, the fine meanings of prepositions, nominal style and comma rules – each chapter with an animated explanation.
levels.wortschatz:A1: Sixteen everyday topics for beginners: introducing yourself, family, health, shopping, travel, work, home, time, weather and numbers.
levels.wortschatz:A2: Thirteen topics for everyday conversations: describing people, renting a flat, housework, driving, shopping, politics, work, public offices, free time and travel.
levels.wortschatz:B1: Ten topics for independent use: feelings and relationships, housing, complaints, school and qualifications, culture, travel, health, the environment, careers and authorities.
levels.wortschatz:C1: Thirteen illustrated advanced vocabulary topics for everyday life, work, study and public life. Each combines English meanings, translated source examples, graded recall, selected-word flashcards and vocabulary games.

chapters.201: Introduce yourself in German: name, origin, age and languages, and the questions you answer on a form or at a registration desk. Ends with a short text about yourself.
chapters.202: Words for parents, siblings, partners and friends, with the possessive articles mein, dein, sein and ihr. Includes short dialogues, a congratulations message and a text about your own family.
chapters.203: Name the parts of the body, say what hurts and phone a doctor's practice. Also covers hygiene and the senses, the two sounds of ch, and a short e-mail saying you are ill.
chapters.204: Everyday errands at the post office, the bank and public offices: letters, accounts and forms, opening times, a voicemail message and a postcard.
chapters.205: Getting around by bus, train and bike: means of transport and their articles, timetables and route plans, separable verbs, and a message saying you will be late.
chapters.206: Travel words for hotels, luggage and tickets: checking in at reception, booking a room by e-mail, choosing a holiday destination and writing a holiday postcard.
chapters.207: Food, quantities and prices for shopping at the supermarket and the market, with a market dialogue and a shopping list.
chapters.208: Ordering and paying in a restaurant or snack bar, reading a menu and answering an invitation – with words for the table, hunger and thirst.
chapters.209: Phones, hobbies and sport: say what you like doing, find out what is on in town and write an e-mail about your free time.
chapters.210: Classroom words and the instructions you meet in a German course, with dialogues in class and a short e-mail to the teacher.
chapters.211: Jobs and the workplace: job titles for men and women, saying what you do with or without an article, reading a job advert and writing a short e-mail about a job.
chapters.212: Rooms, furniture and rent: describe a flat, read a flat advert, view a flat in a dialogue and write an e-mail about your new home.
chapters.213: Telling the time, the days of the week, heute, gestern and morgen, and how often you do something. Arrange an appointment and describe your day.
chapters.214: Months, seasons, dates and the weather: read a weather report, talk about the weather where you live and write a postcard.
chapters.215: The small words that hold sentences together: prepositions of place, und, oder and aber, ja, nein and doch, mit, ohne and für, and words like auch, nur, sehr, noch and schon.
chapters.216: Numbers, prices, measurements and weights: reading and writing numbers, simple sums, metres, litres and kilos, and common abbreviations.
chapters.221: Asking, answering, apologising and declining politely, with verbs that take prepositions, reflexive verbs, and the difference between polite and impolite phrasing.
chapters.222: Describing people's character and appearance with adjectives such as freundlich, geduldig and ehrlich, their opposites, and phrases for saying who looks like whom.
chapters.223: At the doctor's, at the pharmacy and in an emergency: describing symptoms, understanding advice on healthy living and writing a sick note.
chapters.224: Renting a flat: abbreviations in flat adverts, tenants and landlords, moving house, the parts of a building and an e-mail to the landlord.
chapters.225: Housework, household appliances and cleaning rotas: say who does what, whether something is clean or dirty, and leave a note for a flatmate.
chapters.226: Driving in German: traffic signs, filling up, parking, giving directions and describing problems with the car.
chapters.227: Shopping for clothes and products: sizes, whether something fits or suits you, packaging, special offers and exchanging an item.
chapters.228: First words for news about elections, taxes and prices: who is who in politics, rising and falling figures, money and headlines.
chapters.229: Apprenticeships, applications and colleagues: reading a job offer, the steps towards a job, working hours and typical phrases at the office.
chapters.230: Applications, identity cards and forms: where to go for what, talking at the counter, emergency numbers, insurance and the meanings of melden.
chapters.231: Concerts, clubs and day trips: plans for the weekend, culture, a football match, hobbies, and saying whether something was boring or exciting.
chapters.232: Landscapes, accommodation and nature: choosing and writing to a guesthouse, describing what you see, and using wo and wohin correctly.
chapters.233: Adverbs that say when, where and how: zuerst, danach and schließlich, how often, gern, lieber and am liebsten, and comparing the past with today.
chapters.241: Character, relationships and feelings, including feelings with prepositions such as sich freuen über, nouns and adjectives from the same word family, and a forum discussion.
chapters.242: Flat adverts, house rules and neighbours: finding the right advert, understanding what is allowed, writing to your neighbours and forming new words.
chapters.243: Describing products and making complaints: writing a complaint, explaining the problem, comparing online reviews and turning verbs into nouns.
chapters.244: School, reports and language skills: how the school system works, completing a CV, describing your language level and the recognition of qualifications.
chapters.245: Making plans, events and the media: reading a cultural programme, arranging to meet, talking about art and theatre, and saying how an event was.
chapters.246: Accommodation and travel: understanding announcements, and managing at the airport, on the train and at a travel agency.
chapters.247: Health in everyday life and in hospital: talking to a doctor, reading a package leaflet, naming illnesses and turning verbs into nouns.
chapters.248: Animals, environmental problems, weather and climate: climate change, protecting the environment, and describing cause and effect.
chapters.249: Applying for jobs, working life and employees' rights: a job advert, a normal working day, a strike and a cover letter.
chapters.250: Authorities, banks and insurance: understanding an official letter, finding the responsible office, dealing with the bank and writing a formal objection.
chapters.261: Everyday German in detail: ways of moving, eating and reacting, plus furniture, clothing, kitchen equipment and tools. Explore illustrated words and idioms, then practise their meanings and authentic contexts.
chapters.262: Describe appearance, personality and feelings precisely, from subtle differences in build to empathy and emotional idioms. Illustrated word cards pair English meanings with attributed examples and graded practice.
chapters.263: Conversations, expressive verbs, idioms and digital media: understand how people speak, share information and stay in contact. Learn words in sourced contexts and practise recalling their meanings.
chapters.264: Vocabulary from field to table: farming, crops, machinery, animals and their sounds, nutrition, spices and food. Use illustrations, translated examples and short graded rounds to build lasting connections.
chapters.265: Understand the language of the body and medicine: anatomy, symptoms, illnesses, treatments and medical specialties. Explore illustrated word cards, English meanings and attributed contexts before practising recall.
chapters.266: Precise vocabulary for work: professional skills, teamwork, qualifications, employment, demographics and the labour market. Learn with translated source examples, flashcards and graded meaning and context rounds.
chapters.267: Describe devices, processes and scientific reasoning: tools, safety, operation, evidence, hypotheses and conclusions. Illustrations and sourced examples connect technical vocabulary to graded recall practice.
chapters.268: The language of public services, infrastructure, energy, transport and logistics, including supply, resources and flows. Explore illustrated words with English meanings and practise them in attested contexts.
chapters.269: Vocabulary for criminal law, court proceedings, employment rights and contracts. Distinguish offences, people and legal actions through English meanings, attributed examples and graded practice.
chapters.270: Discuss democracy, institutions, elections, ideologies and political attitudes precisely. Illustrated concepts and translated source examples support practice with political vocabulary and fixed expressions.
chapters.271: Vocabulary for history, culture, society, academic discussion and changing trends. Connect words to illustrations and attributed examples, then practise their meanings and contextual forms.
chapters.272: Words for arithmetic, geometry, logic, arguments and conclusions, including mathematical idioms. Diagrams, English meanings and authentic contexts support short graded practice rounds.
chapters.273: Distinguish forms of pay, banking, spending, investment and economic trends. Illustrated word cards, English meanings and attributed examples lead into flashcards, games and graded recall practice.
chapters.1: The German subject pronouns ich, du, er, sie, es, wir, ihr and sie/Sie: when to say du and when Sie, and how a pronoun replaces a noun.
chapters.2: Present-tense endings of regular verbs – ich wohne, du wohnst, er wohnt – and simple sentences built with them.
chapters.3: The three verbs every beginner needs: the forms of sein, haben and möchten, and when to use which.
chapters.4: Verbs that change their vowel in the du and er/sie/es forms, such as essen – isst, fahren – fährt and lesen – liest.
chapters.5: The forms of the modal verbs können, müssen, dürfen, wollen, sollen and möchten, and the sentence bracket: modal verb in position 2, infinitive at the end.
chapters.6: Talking about what you can do and what you want with können, wollen and möchten.
chapters.7: Obligation and permission with müssen, sollen and dürfen – and the important difference between nicht müssen and nicht dürfen.
chapters.8: Separable verbs such as einkaufen and anrufen: the prefix moves to the end of the sentence.
chapters.9: Instructions and requests with the imperative – Komm!, Kommt!, Kommen Sie! – including separable verbs and polite requests.
chapters.10: The question words wer, wie, wo, was, woher, wann and more, and the word order of W-questions.
chapters.11: Yes/no questions with the verb first, and how to answer with ja, nein or doch.
chapters.12: The basic rule of German word order: the verb is the second element, even when the sentence starts with a time or a place.
chapters.13: Sentences with two verbs, such as Ich gehe einkaufen, and where the second verb goes.
chapters.14: How German nouns form the plural – with -e, -er, -n, -s or an umlaut – das Buch, die Bücher.
chapters.15: The definite articles der, das and die and the indefinite ein and eine, and when a noun is new or already known.
chapters.16: Saying no with nicht and kein: which one to use, and the forms of kein.
chapters.17: The accusative case for the direct object – den, einen, keinen – and how to tell subject from object.
chapters.18: The dative case: dem, der and den, short forms such as zum and im, and the dative plural.
chapters.19: The possessive articles mein, dein, sein, ihr, unser, euer and Ihr: choosing between sein and ihr and adding the right ending.
chapters.20: Asking and pointing with welcher? and dieser in every gender.
chapters.21: The object pronouns mich, mir, dich, dir, ihn, ihm and the rest: accusative or dative, also after prepositions.
chapters.22: Verbs with two objects, where someone (dative) gets something (accusative), and the word order when the objects are nouns or pronouns.
chapters.23: Verbs that take a dative object, such as helfen, danken and gefallen.
chapters.24: Asking about people and things in every case with wer, wen, wem and was.
chapters.25: Talking about the past with war and hatte, the simple past of sein and haben.
chapters.26: The perfect tense with haben and the past participle: Ich habe gekocht.
chapters.27: The perfect tense with sein for verbs of movement and change, and how to choose between haben and sein.
chapters.28: Forming the past participle: with and without ge-, regular and irregular, and with separable prefixes.
chapters.29: The simple past of the modal verbs: ich konnte, musste, durfte, wollte and sollte.
chapters.30: Which past tense to use when you talk about yesterday, and why spoken German prefers the perfect for most verbs.
chapters.31: Verbs with sich, such as sich waschen and sich freuen, and the reflexive pronouns.
chapters.32: Time expressions with um, am and im: um acht, am Montag, im Mai.
chapters.33: The prepositions that always take the dative – aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von and zu – with their articles and short forms.
chapters.34: The prepositions that always take the accusative: für, durch, ohne, gegen and um.

chapters.38: Saying where you are with bei, in and auf: beim Arzt, in Berlin.
chapters.39: Saying where you come from with aus and von, and the full set of wohin, wo and woher.

chapters.41: Ordinal numbers and dates: der erste Mai, am ersten Mai.
chapters.42: Comparing with the comparative and als, and with so … wie: größer als, so groß wie.
chapters.43: The superlative in both forms: am schnellsten and der, die, das größte.
chapters.44: Joining main clauses with und, aber, oder and denn, and when to use sondern instead of aber.
chapters.45: Connecting adverbs for consequence and order, such as deshalb, sonst, dann and danach – and why the verb comes straight after them.
chapters.46: Subordinate clauses with weil, dass and wenn, where the verb goes to the end – and the difference between weil and denn.
chapters.47: Compound nouns such as der Regenschirm: how they are built and why the last part decides the article.
chapters.48: Short phrases for states with sein, such as an sein, aus sein and weg sein, and the verbs that bring those states about.
chapters.49: Rules that help you predict der, die or das from a noun's ending or meaning – and the most important exceptions.
chapters.50: The small words denn, doch and mal that make spoken German sound friendly and natural.
chapters.51: Making new words with endings such as -chen, -in and -ung, and what each ending tells you about the article.
chapters.52: Precise negation with nicht, nichts, noch nicht and nicht mehr, and how they answer questions with schon and noch.
chapters.53: Adverbs of place and direction such as oben, unten, vorne and hinten, and nach oben and nach unten.
chapters.54: The simple past of regular and irregular verbs, the tense of stories and written texts.
chapters.55: The past perfect for what happened before another past event: Ich hatte schon gegessen.
chapters.56: Reflexive pronouns in the dative – Ich wasche mir die Hände – and when to use mich or mir.
chapters.57: Separable and inseparable prefixes, such as einkaufen and bestellen, in the present tense and the perfect.
chapters.58: Verbs with fixed prepositions, such as sich freuen über, warten auf and denken an, and the case each one needs.
chapters.59: da- and wo- words such as dafür, daran and worauf: how to refer to things and ask about them, and why people need a preposition with a pronoun.

chapters.66: lassen for having something done by someone else – Ich lasse das Auto reparieren – and its other meanings.

chapters.72: Polite indirect questions with ob and question words: Wissen Sie, ob …? Können Sie mir sagen, wann …?

chapters.78: Time clauses with während, bevor, nachdem and seit: what happens before, after, during or since something else.
chapters.79: Expressing purpose with um … zu and damit, and which one fits when.
chapters.80: Two-part connectors: entweder … oder, weder … noch, sowohl … als auch and nicht nur … sondern auch.

chapters.86: Where the verb goes in German main clauses, questions and imperatives, what can stand in position 1, and how to vary the start of a sentence.

chapters.91: Where nicht goes: negating the whole sentence or just one part, and contrasting with sondern.

chapters.144: Adjective endings in all four cases after the definite article, after the indefinite article and with no article.
chapters.146: Comparative and superlative forms, irregular comparisons and expressions such as einer der besten.

chapters.153: Clauses of consequence with so dass and so … dass.
